The CoworkingView Price Index publishes what flexible office space costs,
city by city: monthly prices for a flex (hot) desk, a fixed desk and a
private office, plus the daily price of a day pass and the hourly price of a
meeting room. The figures are medians and quartiles of the prices listed on
[coworkingview.com](https://coworkingview.com/en/tools/price-index), and they
are open data under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence.

This vignette shows how to read the index with **coworkingview**, compare
cities, and find spaces behind the numbers.

> The code below needs an internet connection, so it is not run when the
> vignette is built. The output shown was produced from real API responses
> of 27 October 2026 (the same responses the package's tests use). Your
> numbers will differ as the index is updated.

```{r}
library(coworkingview)
```

## The index in one call

`cwv_rates()` returns one row per city and product. Monthly products come
with the 25th and 75th percentiles; `sample_size` tells you how many prices
are behind each figure, and `low_confidence` flags figures based on fewer
than ten.

```{r}
rates <- cwv_rates()
monthly <- rates[rates$unit == "month", ]
monthly[, c("city_slug", "currency", "product", "median", "p25", "p75",
            "sample_size", "low_confidence")]
#> # A tibble: 9 x 8
#>   city_slug currency product        median   p25   p75 sample_size low_confidence
#>   <chr>     <chr>    <chr>           <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>       <int> <lgl>
#> 1 abu-dhabi AED      flex_desk        1400  1400  1800           3 TRUE
#> 2 abu-dhabi AED      fix_desk         1800  1800  1800           2 TRUE
#> 3 abu-dhabi AED      private_office   2057  1486  2629           2 TRUE
#> 4 berlin    EUR      flex_desk         214   199   292          72 FALSE
#> 5 berlin    EUR      fix_desk          310   290   421          60 FALSE
#> 6 berlin    EUR      private_office    480   399   550          59 FALSE
#> 7 madrid    EUR      flex_desk         175   130   199          13 FALSE
#> 8 madrid    EUR      fix_desk          260   249   280           9 TRUE
#> 9 madrid    EUR      private_office    385   275   449           9 TRUE
```

A private office price is per office per month, not per person; a flex desk
is a membership for one person.

Day passes and meeting rooms have their own units:

```{r}
rates[rates$unit %in% c("day", "hour"),
      c("city_slug", "product", "unit", "median", "sample_size")]
#> # A tibble: 4 x 5
#>   city_slug product      unit  median sample_size
#>   <chr>     <chr>        <chr>  <dbl>       <int>
#> 1 berlin    day_pass     day       35          59
#> 2 berlin    meeting_room hour      32          79
#> 3 madrid    day_pass     day       22          11
#> 4 madrid    meeting_room hour      28           8
```

## Comparing cities in one currency

Each city is priced in its local currency. To compare across currencies, ask
the API to convert (rates are approximate):

```{r}
cwv_rates(city = "berlin", currency = "USD")[
  , c("product", "unit", "currency", "median", "p25", "p75")]
#> # A tibble: 5 x 6
#>   product        unit  currency median   p25   p75
#>   <chr>          <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 flex_desk      month USD         233   216   317
#> 2 fix_desk       month USD         337   315   458
#> 3 private_office month USD         522   434   598
#> 4 day_pass       day   USD          38    NA    NA
#> 5 meeting_room   hour  USD          35    NA    NA
```

With base R you can reshape the monthly figures to one row per city:

```{r}
eur <- cwv_rates(currency = "EUR")
wide <- reshape(
  as.data.frame(eur[eur$unit == "month", c("city_slug", "product", "median")]),
  idvar = "city_slug", timevar = "product", direction = "wide"
)
wide[order(wide$median.flex_desk), ]
```

and plot the spread of flex desk prices, using the interquartile range to
show how much prices vary within each city:

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3}
flex <- eur[eur$product == "flex_desk" & !eur$low_confidence, ]
flex <- flex[order(flex$median), ]
plot(flex$median, seq_len(nrow(flex)), xlim = range(flex$p25, flex$p75),
     yaxt = "n", pch = 19, xlab = "Flex desk, EUR per month", ylab = "")
segments(flex$p25, seq_len(nrow(flex)), flex$p75, seq_len(nrow(flex)))
axis(2, at = seq_len(nrow(flex)), labels = flex$city_name, las = 1)
```

## Which cities are covered?

`cwv_cities()` lists every city in the index. `entry_median` is the median
of the cheapest monthly option of each space: a good single number for "what
does it cost to get a desk here".

```{r}
cities <- cwv_cities()
cities[, c("city_slug", "published", "property_count",
           "entry_median", "entry_min", "entry_max")]
#> # A tibble: 4 x 6
#>   city_slug    published property_count entry_median entry_min entry_max
#>   <chr>        <lgl>              <int>        <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 abu-dhabi    TRUE                   2         1453      1069      7535
#> 2 berlin       TRUE                  85          265        80      2100
#> 3 madrid       TRUE                  10          325        85      1980
#> 4 example-town FALSE                 NA           NA        NA        NA
```

Cities with `published = FALSE` do not have enough prices yet; they have no
rows in `cwv_rates()`.

## Crediting the source

The licence asks you to credit CoworkingView when you publish the figures.
The exact text travels with every result:

```{r}
cwv_attribution(rates)
#> [1] "Source: CoworkingView Price Index (https://coworkingview.com/en/tools/price-index), as of October 2026. Licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Aggregated figures only; no endorsement by CoworkingView or any operator is implied."
cwv_attribution(rates, "as_of")
#> [1] "2026-10-27T21:06:48.313Z"
```

Put it in the caption of a chart or under a table.

## From the index to the spaces

`cwv_spaces()` searches the catalogue behind the index: coworking spaces,
event spaces, meeting rooms and virtual offices. It returns each space's
position against the city median and a link to its page.

```{r}
spaces <- cwv_spaces(city = "berlin", product = "flex_desk", limit = 3)
spaces[, c("title", "zone_slug", "market_verdict", "url")]
```

`cwv_space()` returns one space with its full pricing table:

```{r}
space <- cwv_space("sankt-oberholz-rosenthaler-berlin")
space$pricing
#> # A tibble: 5 x 8
#>   product        title             price currency billing_period price_on_request
#>   <chr>          <chr>             <dbl> <chr>    <chr>          <lgl>
#> 1 flex_desk      Coworking Member~   209 EUR      month          FALSE
#> 2 fix_desk       Fixed Desk           NA <NA>     month          TRUE
#> 3 private_office Private Team Room    NA <NA>     month          TRUE
#> 4 meeting_room   Meeting & Worksh~    NA <NA>     once           TRUE
#> 5 virtual_office Virtual Office w~    69 EUR      month          FALSE
#> # i 2 more variables: min_capacity <int>, max_capacity <int>
```

The catalogue can be searched and linked to, but not bulk-copied: a call
returns at most 200 spaces, and the descriptions and photos (which belong to
the operators) are never returned. Link to the `url` column instead.
